newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end little changed, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end little changed, seen stable.

text.p: Taiwan share prices wavered only narrowly and ended little changed on Monday with buying focused on petrochemicals and blue chips. Brokers said they expected narrow-range trading to continue in the near term.
The weighted index gained 2.23 points or 0.03 percent to close at 6,891.42. Turnover was a modest T$54.7 billion.
Petrochems jumped on rising overseas styrene monomer prices. Grand Petrochemical and Taiwan Styrene Monomer jumped the daily seven percent limit to T$27.9 and T$34.2 respectively.
"The price hike news is not enough to boost an overall rally," said Foremost analyst Eric Chou.
Caution below the 7,000-point psychological barrier and expected rising year-end liquidity demand also kept investors from entering the market, brokers said.

"There has not been not much buying these days but selling is not great either because the economy is expected to pick up further in the first quarter after it began to recover in the fourth quarter of this year," Chou said.
Low-priced textiles attracted buying interest, with Yu Foong Spinning limit up at T$31.2 and Hualon rising 90 cents or 3.67 percent at T$25.

"Many foreign brokers are on holiday and major local players usually slow down their stock activities when the year-end approaches, so we may not see big movements in share prices for the rest of December unless some breaking news emerges," said Michael Hung, head of research of Nikko Securities.
Brokers agreed that various key sectors would rise in turns to support the market and it was unlikely that the index would find the momentum to climb above 7,000 points in the near term.
